injuries.name: Bramble Foot
injuries.description: An infection of the foot caused by loose plant bramble digging into the feet. Speed is halved and the character takes 1d4 damage per mile walked.

injuries.name: Desert Lung
injuries.description: Harsh inflammation from the hot, dry air. Causes exhaustion and halves speed.

injuries.name: Ergot Poisoning
injuries.description: Fungal poisoning from spoiled rations. Causes disadvantage on cognitive, mental, and social rolls.

injuries.name: Dehydration
injuries.description: Parched to the point of feeling dry inside. Gain 1 level of exhaustion. Cured by using a water resource.

injuries.name: Hyperhydrositis
injuries.description: Rapid production of water in the body. It may be collected to drink, but it is contaminated and spreads the disease. Take 1d6 piercing damage each day until the 1d4-day infection ends.

injuries.name: Twisted Ankles
injuries.description: Speed is halved.

injuries.name: Sun Rash
injuries.description: A burning rash caused by traveling in the heat. Take 1d6 fire damage per mile until taking a short rest in the shade or using a water resource to cool the rash.

injuries.name: Open Wound
injuries.description: Wrap or heal the wound as soon as possible. Roll 1d4; the wound becomes infected after that many days if untreated.

injuries.name: Infected Wound
injuries.description: Requires an open wound. Take 1d6 poison damage each day until healed. Roll 1d4; the wound becomes engorged after that many days if untreated.

injuries.name: Engorged Wound
injuries.description: Requires an infected wound. Take 1d8 poison damage and gain 1 level of exhaustion each day until healed, or until the wound heals naturally in 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Plantar Fasciitis
injuries.description: Plant-like wounds spread over the body during 1d12 days. Take 1d4 piercing damage each day. If not cured before the duration ends, the character becomes a mothering plant whose spores allow food-producing plants to grow.

injuries.name: Heat Melancholy
injuries.description: Depression caused by the overbearing heat. The afflicted character can do nothing more than walk, eat, and sleep for 1d4 days. A profound event has a 50% chance to break the melancholy.

injuries.name: Major Heat Melancholy
injuries.description: Major depression caused by the overbearing heat. The afflicted character can do nothing more than walk, eat, and sleep for 1d8 days. A profound event has a 25% chance to break the melancholy.

injuries.name: Minor Fall
injuries.description: The character falls while traveling and takes 1d4 damage.

injuries.name: Major Fall
injuries.description: The character falls while traveling and takes 1d8 damage.

injuries.name: Blistering Heart
injuries.description: The afflicted character must avoid the sun or gain 2 levels of exhaustion as their heart works twice as hard. Cured in 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Sandy Eyes
injuries.description: Coarse sand blurs the character's vision. Vision is halved for 1 day, or the condition may be cured with 1 water resource.

injuries.name: Dislocated Finger
injuries.description: Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks involving the hands for 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Heavy Packs (Dislocated Collarbone)
injuries.description: Disadvantage on attack rolls and carrying capacity is halved until healed or for 1d6 days.

injuries.name: Nagging Pain
injuries.description: Halve the HP and Hit Dice recovered while resting for 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Heat Exhaustion
injuries.description: Take 1d4 heat damage each day for 1d4 days. Using a water resource cures it.

injuries.name: Scorched Wind
injuries.description: The character may take only one action per turn, or gain 1 level of exhaustion for every second action taken.

injuries.name: Dazed
injuries.description: The character cannot take reactions for 1d6 days.

injuries.name: Dizzy Temples
injuries.description: Disadvantage on Intelligence- and Wisdom-based checks and saves for 1d8 days.

injuries.name: Pulled Rib
injuries.description: Disadvantage on Athletics and Acrobatics checks and saves for 1d8 days.

injuries.name: Solar Berserk
injuries.description: Make one attack against the closest target.

injuries.name: Pale Tongue
injuries.description: The character cannot speak until using an extra water resource to lubricate their tongue.

injuries.name: Sun Crotch
injuries.description: A burning sensation in the loins halves speed for 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Helio-Dreams
injuries.description: Nightmares last for 1d12 days. Before each rest, make a DC 12 Intelligence save or gain 1 level of exhaustion for each nightmare experienced. Exhaustion resets when this condition ends.

injuries.name: Eclipse Wokeness
injuries.description: Sleepless nights last for 1d12 days. Before each rest, make a DC 16 Intelligence save or gain 1 level of exhaustion for each sleepless night. Exhaustion resets when this condition ends.

injuries.name: Coronal Twitches
injuries.description: For 1d6 days, whenever holding an item, make a DC 12 Strength save or drop it. This includes combat.

injuries.name: Sun Ulcers
injuries.description: The character cannot eat without vomiting blood. Each time they eat, they take 1d6 damage, but do not suffer the effects of not eating. Lasts 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Heat Tremors
injuries.description: Uncontrollable tremors from exhaustion or prolonged heat exposure. Disadvantage on Dexterity skills and saves. Resting in the shade ends the condition.

injuries.name: Hair Cut
injuries.description: The character cuts their hair. Whether they like it is up to them. This is flavor only.

injuries.name: Minor Scar
injuries.description: A new scar appears. Funny - the character has not seen that one before.

injuries.name: Adrenaline Rush
injuries.description: The heat has the character on edge. Gain +5 to attacks, but the character cannot heal for 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Dune Ear
injuries.description: Disadvantage on Perception checks.

injuries.name: Cravings for Alcohol
injuries.description: The character wants a drink. Find an alcoholic beverage or suffer disadvantage on skill checks. Each occurrence makes the character more dependent on alcohol.

injuries.name: Barren Psychosis
injuries.description: The character feels that everyone is lying and cannot trust them. Relieved by a Grand Meal, alcohol, or 1d6 days of rest.

injuries.name: Bristle Bones
injuries.description: Spiny projections erupt from the skin and protect against heat exposure. Take 1d8 piercing damage whenever one erupts. Permanently gain +1 Armor, but suffer disadvantage on Charisma rolls. Removing them causes another 1d8 damage.

injuries.name: Busted Kneecap
injuries.description: Speed is halved for 1 day.

injuries.name: Chapped Lips
injuries.description: Disadvantage on Charisma rolls and saves for 1 day.

injuries.name: Cactus Splinter
injuries.description: Take 1d4 damage.

injuries.name: Hallucinogenic Cactus Splinter
injuries.description: Take 1d8 damage and suffer disadvantage on skill rolls.

injuries.name: Cracked Feet
injuries.description: Take 1d4 damage each day for 1d4 days.

injuries.name: Cracked Hands
injuries.description: For 1 day, make a DC 12 Dexterity save or drop any object held in the hands.

injuries.name: Thirsty
injuries.description: Lose 1 water resource.

injuries.name: Hungry
injuries.description: Lose 1 food resource.

injuries.name: Tired
injuries.description: The character must automatically take 1 day of rest.

injuries.name: Exhausted
injuries.description: The character must rest for a number of days until they succeed on a DC 14 Constitution save.

events: A deserted sand rider could be repaired and used for 1d6 days before breaking down. It can carry injured party members and doubles group movement.
The party encounters members of the Cult of Eyes, who give directions to their covenant.
The party finds a puddle of water. Make a Survival roll to determine whether it is contaminated.
A random shack shop stands where it absolutely should not be.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
Two giant scorpions attack.
The party meets another Exodus group that is dying and sick. Do they spare 2 food and 3 water resources?
An abandoned salt mine may be worked for extra money. Roll 1d12; the result is the amount of silver earned.
Shifted sands reveal an old chest containing a map marked with an X and a dagger.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A sandstorm strikes. Seek cover or make a DC 16 Strength save; on a failure, the character is sucked into the storm and takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage.
An oasis holds an enslaved marid. It grants a boon - a free feat - to anyone who frees it. The water is contaminated but collectable.
A cactus grove contains 1d6 dragon fruits and 1d4 hallucinogenic fruits.
Three giant desert wasps attack.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
Four pieces of rare, volatile solite cling to a rock. Each piece requires a DC 15 Sleight of Hand check to harvest. On a failure, that piece explodes for 4d6 radiant damage and is destroyed.
Survivalist bandits ambush passersby from the dunes, perhaps using a citizen in distress as a lure. The group includes 3 sword bandits and 2 archer bandits.
Three sand hag sisters offer blessings in return for 1 food and 1 water resource. If given bad food or water, the blessing becomes a curse.
The party finds hot springs that heal every player for 3d8 HP.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A mirage of a beautiful palace leads the party off course, as determined by the GM.
A strange old man offers a story about a floating castle for 1 food resource.
A kind old lady gives the party 2 food and 2 water resources. The food appears great but is spoiled, and the water is contaminated.
A wandering trader appears.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A giant floating skull attacks.
A black obsidian obelisk calls for a sacrifice in exchange for a permanent boon. A reader who refuses suffers a permanent 1d6 reduction to maximum health.
The party witnesses a lonely stranger undergoing Plantar Fasciitis. Can they stomach collecting and eating the food the person provides?
An evil Exodus group attacks: 1 paladin, 2 sorcerers, and 2 fighters.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A wandering trader appears.
The party enters a field of large glass sculptures. Each piece burdens the party but can be sold for 50 silver.
A flying herd of camels blesses the party with their unique third eyes and heals everyone for 2d4 HP.
Solar winds sweep through. Find shelter or take 2d6 fire damage and catch fire. Use a water resource to extinguish the flames or take another 2d6 fire damage.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
An ancient tomb lies beneath the sand. The first character to discover and open it permanently learns one level 1 spell of their choice and may cast it once per day.
Three Cult of the Eyes occultists attack, and a mark leading to their covenant is placed.
A skeletal dragon comes alive and will find the party in 1d4 days. For now, tell the players: Nothing happens.
Three bandits raid the party. A DC 14 Charisma save can turn the fight into a trade instead.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A rainstorm breaks the drought. The party may collect 4 clean water resources.
A wandering trader appears.
A successful DC 15 Survival check while hunting gains the party 2 food resources.
A burrowing worm attacks. Defeating it gains the party 4 food resources.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A flyer for an unknown circus appears, with its location marked on the map.

The party finds a small citadel built from junk and inhabited by friendly scavengers. If the party accepts their hospitality, a sandstorm strikes and raiders on horseback attack. The entire town dies.
The party meets desert monks on a spiritual journey. They are starving and thirsty but refuse food and water, insisting the land will provide. One falls from exhaustion. What does the party do?
Petrified roots of an ancient tree cover half a square mile. Well-cut slices are extremely valuable, but producing them requires specialized equipment or magic; chips are nearly worthless.
Heavenly light heals the party to full, removes exhaustion, and ends hunger. Someone - or something - seems to appear in the light.
The party finds a small oasis. Drinking its water causes all hair on a character's body to fall out.
Vultures feast on a dead baby camel that appears to have died of natural causes.
Fire spouts erupt from the sand, dealing 1d4 fire damage to the party.
A wandering trader appears.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
The ribs of an ancient boat shelter nomads. Casks of old, contaminated water lie half-buried nearby.
Four sand dwarves spring from an ambush, having mistaken the party for raiders. They have dried, spiced meat to trade.
The party finds a sand-filled warforged. Cleaning it out brings it to life, and it becomes the party's bodyguard.
A buzzard aarakocra follows the party, shouting, 'Hurry up! I'm starving over here!'
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A strange boulder in the distance proves to be a gigantic sculpted hand of stone, jade, or another material. Enemies may nest on it, or traps may surround it.
Sinking sand requires a Perception check to spot and Dexterity and Strength saving throws to escape. Failure leaves a character stuck for an entire day.
A 30-foot-tall tortoise crosses the land with scaffolding and a small camp on its shell. Notes and food welcome visitors and encourage them to leave something for the next traveler.
A wandering merchant appears.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A small hut stands beside a large cavern whose chambers and tunnels connect to it. Two burned skeletons lie at the entrance.
At a grove of reddish sand, odd trees, and a white flag, tentacles wave from the earth. A xorn rises and offers meat and water in exchange for gems and metal.

A male fire genasi and two winged female tieflings fight two giant tarantulas. They will not survive without help. In thanks, they give the party an amulet of fire resistance, collect the venom, and disappear through a portal to Hell.
The party discovers the Sex Hut. Embarrassing or refreshing? That is up to them.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A beggar and a princess fly past on a magic carpet.
A desperate or negligent party member cuts open a cactus and learns that this species ejects its needles forcefully when touched.
A Mongolian death worm spits acid at the party for 1d4 damage before retreating beneath the sand.
A wandering merchant appears.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
Ruby mines may be worked with Survival. Each ruby is worth 10 silver. A critical failure, or taking more than four rubies, collapses the mine for 3d10 damage.
A reptilian person throws a slab of meat at a party member and walks away. Gain 1 food resource.

Four potions marked 'Drink me' stand before the party. Red grants fire resistance and heals a sun injury; green deals 2d4 poison damage; blue heals 1d6 HP; black has an equal chance of blessing or curse. Drinking one counts as a water resource.
A gnoll tribe claims to have abandoned violence for hermitage but has been harassed by settlements because of nearby hostile tribes. Can the party settle the problem without violence?
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A wandering trader appears.
The party finds a puddle of water. Roll to determine contamination.
A sweet rainstorm fills 4 water resources.
A broken sand skiff abandoned by lizardfolk nomads contains 3 fire-starting glass lenses, 2 spears, and half a barrel of water.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
The party hears slithering, scraping, and rushing air. Over the next dune, a gigantic sand worm races past, oblivious to them.
War drums sound very close, but the party is actually walking on drum sand.
A wandering trader appears.
A single purple flower grows in the desert. Detecting magic reveals a low aura of alteration that dissipates if the flower is picked.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
A bottled djinn is found among the skeletal remains of a human nomad and his pet monkey.
Dragonborn worship the dried, sun-bleached bones of a dragon. They will trade if treated respectfully.
A cave in a dry lakebed contains ten tritons preserved in caked-mud stasis from when the land still had water.
The party encounters followers from a nearby village who worship the rays of the sun god.
Roll on the Injury & Disease table.
Wet sand that smells like cinnamon can be harvested and sold for 50 bronze per pound in the next populated area.
An oasis is rigged with magical traps. Promising flowers and edible plants trigger fireball or poison-gas traps when picked.
A mummy has awakened beneath the ground. Dead plants and desiccated animals litter the area, whispers ride the wind, and sleepers suffer dark dreams of something calling.
A caravan of silk traders offers to hire the party as extra guards. They are already traveling in the same direction.
A sandstorm grows into a massive cyclone. At its center, a face offers to carry the party anywhere the sky can reach. The journey may hurt; the landing is up to the travelers.
